cards.explanation: The answer is False. It's the reverse of a warning. Jehu says, “…do not let anyone escape from the city to go and tell it in Jezreel.” (2 Kings 9:15) That's his instruction to the commanders, friends. He doesn't want word going ahead to Jezreel.

The answer is Ahaziah king of Judah. The text says Ahaziah king of Judah had gone down to see Joram (2 Kings 9:16). Joram is laid up in Jezreel, so Ahaziah is basically visiting a patient. Jehu is about to crash that visit.

The answer is whether they come in peace. Joram tells his men, “Send him out to meet them and ask, ‘Have you come in peace?’…” (2 Kings 9:17) Simple question, friends, but it's about to get a very strange answer. I think Joram expected a plain yes or no.

The answer is that Jehu tells the horseman to fall in behind him. Jehu says, “What do you know about peace?” and then, “Fall in behind me.” (2 Kings 9:18) Joram's rider came with a question about peace and got that answer. Then the watchman reports, “The messenger reached them, but he is not coming back.” (2 Kings 9:18)

The answer is True. The watchman says the charioteer “…is driving like Jehu son of Nimshi…” (2 Kings 9:20). He recognizes the driving style from way up on that tower. I'd be nervous if somebody recognized my driving from that far away.

The answer is that Joram rides out in his own chariot. Joram shouts, “Harness!” and they harness his chariot (2 Kings 9:21). Then Joram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah set out, each in his own chariot. They meet Jehu on the property of Naboth the Jezreelite.

The answer is Jezebel's idolatry and witchcraft. Jehu says, “How can there be peace… as long as the idolatry and witchcraft of your mother Jezebel abound?” (2 Kings 9:22) Jezebel is Joram's mother, friends. So Joram asks a yes or no question and gets a no, with a reason.

The answer is flees. Joram asks, “Have you come in peace, Jehu?” and Jehu answers about the idolatry and witchcraft of Joram's mother Jezebel (2 Kings 9:22). Then Joram turns around and flees, calling out, “Treachery, Ahaziah!” (2 Kings 9:23) I think that answer told him this was no friendly visit.

The answer is that Jehu tells Bidkar to throw the body into Naboth's field. Jehu tells Bidkar his officer, “Pick him up and throw him into the field of Naboth the Jezreelite.” (2 Kings 9:25) This is heavy, so I'll say it plainly. Jehu ties it to what the LORD said about repaying on that plot of ground (2 Kings 9:26).

The answer is True. Jehu says, “Now then, according to the word of the LORD, pick him up and throw him on the plot of ground.” (2 Kings 9:26) He points back to what the LORD declared about the blood of Naboth and his sons. The LORD's word is what Jehu points to.

The answer is “Shoot him too!” Jehu pursued Ahaziah, shouting those words (2 Kings 9:27). The word too comes right after Joram was shot. Then they shot Ahaziah in his chariot on the Ascent of Gur, near Ibleam.

The answer is Jerusalem. His servants carried Ahaziah by chariot to Jerusalem and buried him with his fathers in his tomb in the City of David (2 Kings 9:28). Before that, he fled to Megiddo and died there (2 Kings 9:27). Jerusalem is where his servants took him, friends.

The answer is that she paints her eyes and watches from a window. The text says Jezebel “…painted her eyes, adorned her head, and looked down from a window.” (2 Kings 9:30) She isn't hiding. I think she wanted to be seen.
The answer is True. Jehu looks up at the window and calls out, “Who is on my side? Who?” (2 Kings 9:32) He repeats that one word, who. And two or three eunuchs look down.
The answer is “Throw her down!” That's what Jehu yells (2 Kings 9:33). I think this one hurts to read, friends. The text says they threw her down.

The answer is king. Jehu says, “Take care of this cursed woman, and bury her, for she was the daughter of a king.” (2 Kings 9:34) That's his reason for the burial. It's a quiet line after a rough scene.

The answer is False. They did not find her whole body. When they went out to bury her, “…they found nothing but her skull, her feet, and the palms of her hands.” (2 Kings 9:35) That's all they find. Then they go back and tell Jehu.

The answer is Elijah the Tishbite. Jehu says the LORD “…spoke through His servant Elijah the Tishbite…” (2 Kings 9:36). The text calls Elijah the LORD's servant. Jehu is saying what happened to Jezebel lines up with what the LORD said.

The answer is True. The word through Elijah says, “…so that no one can say: This is Jezebel.” (2 Kings 9:37) That's how Jehu quotes it, friends. Just before that line, the word says Jezebel's body will lie like dung in the field (2 Kings 9:37).
